rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods / Results (Figures 1-8) report the authors' own laboratory experiments on hydrogen nanobubble water, ROS removal in vitro and oxidative stress in Tetrahymena thermophila exposed to copper.
rows.notes: The study is a laboratory toxicology/chemistry study of hydrogen nanobubble water scavenging reactive oxygen species and alleviating copper toxicity in a single-celled ciliate. It involves no irrigation system, no drip or aerated drip irrigation, no crops, no yield or crop quality measurement. It provides no evidence of its own on ADI increasing crop yield or quality compared with conventional drip irrigation; the only link is that it concerns nanobubble water, a component of some aerated irrigation systems.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods / Results (Figures 1-8) report the authors' own laboratory experiments on hydrogen nanobubble water, ROS removal and antioxidant enzyme activity/gene expression in Tetrahymena thermophila under copper stress.
rows.notes: The study does not involve drip or aerated drip irrigation, crops, pests, diseases or pesticide applications. It shows that hydrogen nanobubble water removes H2O2, superoxide and hydroxyl radicals in vitro and reduces copper-induced oxidative stress in a ciliate protozoan. Nothing in it addresses reduced pesticide use or pest control under ADI versus conventional drip irrigation.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references).
